contentEn:
Your Budget Is Already Wrong Before You Sign Anything

Every experienced project manager in Vancouver hears the same line from homeowners on day one: "We have $X saved and that's our budget." Within weeks, that number routinely grows by 20-40%. The reason is not poor planning — it is the nature of existing Metro Vancouver homes, most of which were built before 1990.

Hidden conditions are the main culprit. Opening up walls during demo frequently reveals knob-and-tube wiring that must be updated to meet BC Safety Authority standards, asbestos in floor tiles or pipe insulation (common in any building material installed before 1990), and structural modifications that require an engineer's stamped drawing before the city will issue a permit. None of these appear in a scope-of-work document you sign at the kitchen table.

Reno Stars project managers budget a 15-25% contingency line for whole-house projects in Vancouver, Burnaby, and Richmond. For a $180,000 renovation, that is $27,000-$45,000 set aside before a single wall comes down. Homeowners who skip this line are the ones who end up making painful mid-project choices — cheaper countertops, deferred landscaping, or a scope that shrinks the moment money runs out.

The Permit Timeline Is Separate From the Build Timeline

Vancouver homeowners frequently assume permits are an upfront gate. They are not — in many cases the city permit review takes 6-14 weeks and runs concurrently with early demolition and material procurement. The critical mistake is waiting for permit approval before ordering long-lead items like custom cabinets, which themselves take 8-12 weeks from deposit to delivery in Metro Vancouver.

For a typical kitchen renovation in Vancouver in 2026, the permitting phase runs alongside the planning phase. A city-issued building permit in Vancouver proper averages 8-12 weeks for a full kitchen reno, according to City of Vancouver permit data. Surrey and Richmond tend toward 4-8 weeks for comparable projects. Delta and Port Moody are generally faster at 3-6 weeks. These numbers are from actual Reno Stars permit records across 14 cities in the Lower Mainland.

The sequence that keeps projects on schedule: engage your contractor, order a structural assessment, submit permit applications, procure long-lead materials in parallel, begin demo only after permit submission — not after approval. Reno Stars uses this overlap on every whole-house project we manage.

Strata Buildings Have Rules That Can Stop Work Entirely

More than 60% of Vancouver-area residents live in strata-titled properties, according to BC Assessment data. Condo and townhouse renovations in Vancouver, Burnaby, Coquitlam, and Richmond are governed by strata corporation bylaws that can prohibit work during certain hours, require specific contractor insurance coverage, mandate noise mitigation plans, and in some buildings prohibit work entirely during statutory holidays.

The most common surprise: a building's strata council must approve any work that affects common property — which in many older Vancouver and Burnaby high-rises includes the space behind the demising wall, all plumbing risers, and anything that touches the exterior envelope. A Reno Stars kitchen renovation in a Metrotown condo required three strata council votes over six weeks before a single contractor entered the unit.

Before signing a purchase agreement on a pre-sale renovation or before starting work in a strata building, obtain the building's full renovation guidelines from the property manager and have your contractor review them line by line.

Living Through a Renovation Is Not a Mild Inconvenience

Contractors and designers sometimes describe renovation disruption as "a bit dusty" or "you'll need to vacate the kitchen for a while." That framing does not prepare you for the reality. A full kitchen renovation in an occupied Vancouver home in 2026 typically means the kitchen is unusable for 4-8 weeks. A bathroom renovation means a single-bathroom home has no functioning bathroom for 2-4 weeks. A whole-house renovation often makes the home unsafe for children under 5 and pets for the demo and rough-in phase.

Reno Stars has managed whole-house renovations where the homeowners stayed on site. It requires clear written boundaries with the contractor, dust barriers at every doorway, and a written schedule of which zones are active each day. It also adds 15-25% to the project timeline because the crew adjusts their schedule around the family's daily routine. The premium is worth it for some families; it is the wrong choice for others.

Asbestos Testing Is Not Optional in Pre-1990 Vancouver Homes

BC occupational health regulations and WorkSafeBC guidelines require asbestos testing before any demolition in a building built before 1990. This is not a contractor preference — it is a legal requirement. A certified asbestos assessor takes samples from accessible wall cavities, floor tiles, pipe wrap, and insulation. Results take 48-72 hours.

If asbestos is present, an abatement contractor must remove it before demo can continue. Costs range from $2,000 to $15,000+ depending on the home's size and the extent of contamination. Reno Stars includes pre-demo asbestos testing as a standard line item in every scope of work for Vancouver and Lower Mainland homes built before 1990. Any contractor who skips this step is exposing you to legal liability and your family to serious health risk.

Your Neighbours Will Be Affected — Tell Them Before the City Does

A building permit in Vancouver becomes a public document. Your neighbours receive no automatic notification — but they will notice the dumpster, the crew of vans parked on the street, and the early-morning truck idling. The homeowners who have the smoothest projects in our experience are the ones who put a note in every neighbour's mailbox before demo starts: a brief description of the work, the expected duration, and a direct phone number for the site supervisor.

In West Vancouver and North Vancouver especially, where lot sizes are larger but neighbour proximity during a major reno is still high, this step prevents formal noise complaints to the city — which can result in work-stop orders pending review. A five-minute courtesy notice costs nothing and has prevented work stoppages on multiple Reno Stars projects.

Material Lead Times Are Longer Than Your Contractor Likely Told You

In 2026, most custom cabinet shops in the Lower Mainland quote 10-14 weeks from sign-off to delivery. Imported porcelain and quartz slabs from Italy, Spain, and Brazil are running 14-20 weeks due to global shipping disruptions that continue to affect Vancouver supply chains. Locally stocked items from stores like Tauras or Superior are faster at 2-4 weeks but have limited SKUs.

Reno Stars maintains relationships with seven Metro Vancouver suppliers and checks real inventory at the time of every design meeting. The number one cause of timeline extensions on Vancouver renovations in our 2025 project records was material delays — not labour availability or permit backlogs. Ask your contractor for a written material procurement schedule, not just a build schedule.

The Most Underrated Renovation Decision: Who Manages the Project

Homeowners often focus on design aesthetics and price-per-square-foot when selecting a renovation company. The more important question is who is on site every day managing the subcontractors, the material deliveries, and the inspector visits. General contractors who sub everything out to independent tradespeople often have no single point of accountability when things go wrong. Design-build firms that employ their own project managers tend to have tighter quality control and faster response times.

Reno Stars employs a dedicated project manager on every whole-house renovation in Vancouver, Richmond, and Burnaby. That person is the homeowner's direct contact from first meeting through final walkthrough. Our clients consistently cite this single point of contact as the most valued part of working with us — more than any design decision or material selection.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much should I budget above my quoted renovation cost in Vancouver?

For a whole-house renovation in Vancouver, budget a 15-25% contingency above the contractor's quote. For a kitchen or bathroom renovation, a 10-20% contingency is typical. Reno Stars project records from across Metro Vancouver in 2025 show the average overrun was 18% on whole-house projects where no contingency was pre-agreed.

How long does a Vancouver kitchen renovation take in 2026?

A full kitchen renovation in Vancouver — including design, permits, demo, rough-in, finishing, and inspection — averages 12-20 weeks for an experienced contractor. Condo kitchens in strata buildings add 4-8 weeks for strata approval processes and shared-element coordination.

Do I need asbestos testing before renovating my Vancouver home?

Yes, legally. Any demolition work in a Vancouver-area home built before 1990 requires a certified asbestos assessment under WorkSafeBC regulations. Reno Stars includes this as a standard pre-demo step for every pre-1990 project we manage.

Can I live in my home during a whole-house renovation?

Yes, with the right mitigation in place. Reno Stars has completed whole-house renovations in occupied Vancouver homes. It requires written dust containment protocols, a dedicated site supervisor, and written agreement on working hours. Budget an additional 15-25% time premium for an occupied renovation versus an empty-home renovation.

What permits does a Vancouver kitchen renovation require?

A full kitchen renovation in Vancouver typically requires a building permit and an electrical permit. If plumbing is relocated, a plumbing permit is also required. Permit costs in Vancouver proper range from $1,500 to $4,500 depending on project valuation. Surrey and Richmond fees differ slightly. Reno Stars manages all permit applications as part of every full-service project.
contentZh:
签合同前你的预算已经是错的

大温哥华每位有经验的项目经理都会在第一天听到同样的话：我们存了X万这就是我们的预算。几周后这个数字通常会增长20-40%。原因不在于规划不足而是大温哥华现有房屋的特性大多数建于1990年之前。隐蔽工程是主要罪魁祸首。拆除时打开墙壁经常会发现必须更新至BC省安全管理局标准的knob-and-tube布线1990年前安装的地砖或管道保温层中可能存在的石棉以及需要工程师盖章图纸才能获得市府许可的结构修改。

Reno Stars项目经理为温哥华本拿比和列治文的整体装修项目预留15-25%的应急资金。对于18万加元的装修项目这是27000-45000加元的预留款在拆除第一面墙之前就已确定。

许可证时间线与施工时间线是分开的

温哥华房主经常认为许可证是一个前置关卡实际上并非如此。在许多情况下城市许可证审核需要6-14周与早期拆除和材料采购并行进行。最关键的错误是在订购长交期材料之前等待许可证批准。2026年温哥华典型厨房装修审批阶段与规划阶段并行。温哥华市区全面厨房装修建筑许可平均需要8-12周。列治文和素里类似项目需要4-8周。三角洲和满地宝通常更快3-6周。这些数字来自Reno Stars在大温哥华14个城市的实际许可记录。

分契物业有规则可能完全阻止施工

根据BC省评估数据超过60%的大温地区居民居住在分契产权物业中。温哥华本拿比高贵林和列治文的公寓和联排别墅装修受分契公司附则管辖可以禁止在特定时间施工要求特定的承包商保险范围要求制定噪音缓解计划在某些建筑中甚至完全禁止在法定节假日施工。最常见的意外是建筑的分契委员会必须批准任何影响公共区域的工程。在预售装修签购房协议之前或在分契建筑开始施工之前从物业经理处获取建筑完整装修指南让您的承包商逐行审查。

住在装修期间不是轻微的不便

承包商和设计师有时将装修干扰描述为有点灰尘或您需要暂时不使用厨房。这种描述无法让您做好准备。2026年在温哥华有人居住的房屋中进行全面厨房装修通常意味着厨房4-8周无法使用。浴室装修意味着一套单卫生间房屋2-4周没有可用的浴室。整体装修往往使5岁以下儿童和宠物在拆除和粗糙装修阶段无法安全待在屋内。

石棉检测在1990年前建成的温哥华房屋中不是可选的

根据BC省职业健康法规和WorkSafeBC指南在1990年前建成的任何建筑进行拆除前必须进行石棉检测。这是法律要求。认证石棉评估员从可触及的墙壁腔体地砖管道保温层和保温材料中取样。结果需要48-72小时。如果存在石棉清理承包商必须在拆除继续之前将其清除。根据房屋大小和污染程度成本从2000加元到15000加元以上不等。

您的邻居会受到影响在城市之前告诉他们

温哥华的建筑许可证是公开文件。您的邻居不会自动收到通知但他们会注意到垃圾箱停在街上的货车队以及清晨卡车的空转。在我们的经验中项目最顺利的房主是在拆除开始前在每位邻居的信箱里放一张便条。特别是在西温哥华和北温哥华这一步骤可以防止向城市提出正式噪音投诉从而导致工作停工待审。

材料交期比您的承包商可能告诉您的要长

2026年低陆平原大多数定制橱柜店的报价从签章到交货需要10-14周。从意大利西班牙和巴西进口的瓷砖和石英石板正在运行14-20周的交期。从Tauras或Superior等本地库存商处订购的商品较快2-4周但SKU有限。Reno Stars与七家大温哥华供应商保持关系。材料延迟是温哥华装修时间延长的首要原因。

最被低估的装修决策是谁管理项目

房主在选择装修公司时通常关注设计美学和每平方英尺的价格。更重要的问题是每天都在现场管理分包商材料交付和检查访问的人。将所有工作外包给独立装修工人的总承包商在事情出错时往往没有单一的问责点。Reno Stars在温哥华列治文和本拿比的每一个整体装修项目中都配备专用项目经理。该人是房主从首次会议到最终验收的直接联系人。

计划进行厨房浴室全屋或商业装修？联系Reno Stars获取免费无义务报价。

常见问题

在温哥华装修我的报价应该上浮多少预算

对于温哥华的整体装修在承包商报价基础上预留15-25%的应急资金。对于厨房或浴室装修10-20%的应急资金是典型的。Reno Stars 2025年整个低陆平原项目记录显示在未预先约定应急资金的项目中平均超支为18%。

2026年温哥华厨房装修需要多长时间

2026年温哥华全面厨房装修包括设计许可拆除粗糙装修收尾和检查对于有经验的承包商平均需要12-20周。分契建筑中的公寓厨房因分契审批流程需要额外增加4-8周。

在装修温哥华房屋之前需要石棉检测吗

是的这是法律要求。根据WorkSafeBC法规1990年前建成的温哥华地区任何建筑进行拆除工程都需要认证石棉评估。

整体装修期间我可以住在家里吗

可以但需要正确的缓解措施。需要书面的防尘协议专用现场主管以及关于工作时间面的书面协议。将装修视为有人居住而非空置的工期溢价增加15-25%。

温哥华厨房装修需要哪些许可证

温哥华全面厨房装修通常需要建筑许可证和电气许可证。如果管道有搬迁还需要管道许可证。温哥华市区的许可证费用根据项目估值从1500加元到4500加元不等。Reno Stars在每个全服务项目中管理所有许可证申请。
